purpose: Source-indexed visual morphology examples for the Hays Botany visual learner. This supplements data/learning-layer.json with real-world examples of plant structures, functions, and field context.
copyright_note: Keep third-party video frames and photos as source links/timestamps unless reuse rights are verified. The public repository should store references, teaching notes, and locally-created diagrams/annotations rather than copied copyrighted media.

workflow.capture: Find a useful moment where a structure is clearly visible or explicitly pointed out.
workflow.index: Record source, timestamp or image reference, term, taxon when known, and what the structure is doing.
workflow.verify: Check the botanical claim against an authoritative botany source before promoting it into the canonical learning layer.
workflow.localize: Whenever possible, attach a Central Texas / target-zone species that shows the same structure.
workflow.teach: Turn the verified example into a visual lesson that prioritizes a real photo, exact part labels/arrows, and a close-up of the diagnostic structure; add a diagram only when it improves understanding.

visual_examples.look_here: At the base of the flower around the sepals.
visual_examples.what_it_is: Specialized nectar-secreting hairs associated with the sepal bases.
visual_examples.why_it_matters_for_id: A useful family-level synapomorphy in Malvaceae.

visual_examples.look_here: In the center of the flower.
visual_examples.what_it_is: Male floral parts fused into a hollow tube surrounding the style.
visual_examples.what_it_is_doing: Positions the anthers around the style while the style and stigma lobes project through the center.
Part of a repeated drought- and nutrient-stress morphology described for cerrado plants.
visual_examples.why_it_matters_for_id: Leaf texture can be a useful vegetative character when combined with attachment and arrangement.

visual_examples.look_here: Where the leaf blade meets the stem.
visual_examples.what_it_is: Sessile leaves attach directly to the stem; petiolate leaves have a leaf stalk.
visual_examples.what_it_is_doing: Describes attachment rather than a process.
visual_examples.why_it_matters_for_id: Presence or absence of a petiole is often immediately diagnostic.

visual_examples.look_here: Follow the stem and watch how adjacent leaves overlap.
visual_examples.what_it_is: Overlapping leaves arranged like shingles or scales.
visual_examples.what_it_is_doing: Describes the spatial arrangement of leaves.
visual_examples.why_it_matters_for_id: A striking architecture character that can narrow unfamiliar plants quickly.

visual_examples.what_it_is: A largely single-stemmed growth habit with foliage concentrated toward the upper portion.
visual_examples.what_it_is_doing: Describes plant architecture rather than an individual organ.
visual_examples.why_it_matters_for_id: Habit can be a strong first-pass field cue before close morphology.

visual_examples.look_here: Between opposite leaf petioles at a node.
visual_examples.what_it_is: A stipule positioned between the petioles of an opposite leaf pair.
visual_examples.what_it_is_doing: Protects or associates with the developing node depending on the taxon.
visual_examples.why_it_matters_for_id: A high-value Rubiaceae-family clue in many taxa.

visual_examples.what_it_is: A corolla with a long narrow tube that abruptly expands into a flat limb.
visual_examples.what_it_is_doing: Flower shape can constrain how pollinators access nectar and contact reproductive structures.
visual_examples.why_it_matters_for_id: Corolla form is useful descriptive morphology.

visual_examples.look_here: Behind or below the perianth at the ovary.
visual_examples.what_it_is: An ovary with flattened longitudinal extensions or wings.
visual_examples.what_it_is_doing: The wings are part of the ovary/fruit architecture.
visual_examples.why_it_matters_for_id: Ovary shape is often more diagnostic than petal color.

visual_examples.look_here: Outer plant surfaces and stomatal structures.
visual_examples.what_it_is: The protective outer tissue system, including epidermal structures such as trichomes and guard cells.
visual_examples.what_it_is_doing: Protecting surfaces and regulating exchange with the environment.
visual_examples.why_it_matters_for_id: Surface hairs and stomatal features can be highly diagnostic at close scale.

visual_examples.look_here: Internal stem/root/leaf vascular bundles; usually requires a section or diagram.
visual_examples.what_it_is_doing: Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals; phloem transports sugars and other photosynthates.
visual_examples.why_it_matters_for_id: More useful for understanding plant function and anatomy than routine field identification.

candidate_queue.task: Do a timestamp pass for sepal, petal/corolla, stamen/anther/filament, pistil/carpel, stigma, style, ovary, fusion, symmetry, and synapomorphy examples.
Visually verify candidate timestamps and capture exact taxa for interpetiolar stipules, salverform corolla, sexually dimorphic corollas, winged ovary, and androphore.
Index examples of epidermis, cuticle, stomatal opening, guard cells, trichomes, ground tissues, xylem, and phloem.
For every verified morphology term, add at least one Central Texas / project-target-zone plant that demonstrates the same structure.

rules: Prefer real photographs whenever the structure can be shown clearly.
Label the exact botanical part rather than relying on a generic caption.
Use arrows or labels added by the learner when the source photo is not already annotated.
When teaching part-versus-whole relationships, reuse the same underlying image with different overlays when practical.
Use macro or close-up views for small diagnostic structures.
Pair a real photograph with a simple drawing only when the diagram improves understanding.
Preserve source provenance and clearly distinguish learner overlays from markings embedded in the source image.
Clarity of the diagnostic structure outranks aesthetics.
